comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral findings (C5-C7, C67). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical significance of behavioral adjustments to reward changes, while peer reviewers did not raise concerns about these control measures confirming task engagement.

Disagreement on SWR rate findings (C8-C18). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with converging evidence from multiple statistical approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing concerns about small sample sizes, small effect sizes, experimental complexity, and need for increased sample sizes and more consistent dosing/timing for reproducibility.

Disagreement on RPE-related modulation findings (C19-C25). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED while acknowledging study limitations (mostly familiar sessions, need for replication). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with one explicitly stating the reward volatility experiment results are 'not fully convincing' and noting the authors' own acknowledgment of need for additional validation.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C39-C41). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes novelty-dependence is well-supported despite acknowledged limitations. Peer reviewers affirm main conclusions about VTA dopamine's critical role during novel learning, with editor stating evidence is 'solid' and provides 'valuable contribution.'

Agreement on replay findings (C31-C38, with peer also including C30). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive evidence for reverse replay specificity to novel environments and experimental animals. Peer reviewers positively evaluated findings, noting VTA's role in spatial memory consolidation and highlighting novel dependency of hippocampal replay on dopamine.

Agreement on place field analysis (C26-C29, with peer also including C30). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes preserved directional coding with modest but significant effects of CNO and novelty. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns, implicitly supporting these foundational neural recording observations through praise of methodological robustness.

Disagreement on methodology validation (C1-C3, with peer also including C65-C66). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate anatomical landmarks and validation criteria. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about need for more rigorous histological validation from all animals and noting small sample sizes and exclusions raise reproducibility concerns.

Disagreement on sample size reporting (C65-C66). OpenEval finds transparent reporting SUPPORTED with appropriate and well-justified exclusions despite modest final sample. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns, noting small sample sizes (n=4 experimental, n=3 control) and exclusions create uncertainty about reproducibility.

Agreement on methodological details (C10, with peer also including C4). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C10 provides context consistent with prior work. Peer reviewers praised methodological robustness and did not raise concerns about these technical details.

Agreement on background literature (C52-C64, with OpenEval R9 covering C42-C51 and peer R9 covering both sets). Both evaluations find citation claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes accurate summarization of foundational literature providing theoretical framework. Peer reviewers did not challenge citation accuracy and implicitly accepted the background as addressing significant gap in understanding.

Agreement on prior literature citations (C42-C48, C50-C51, overlapping with peer's broader C42-C64 coverage). Both evaluations find claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate context for interpreting findings regarding VTA suppression magnitude and novelty-related dopamine activity. Peer reviewers accepted these as accurate representations of prior work.

Agreement on theoretical interpretation (C49). Both evaluations find claim SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is well-established hypothesis providing mechanistic context. Peer reviewers included this among accepted background citations without challenge.
